The nomination form then shows the platform blocked by iN with no way to act, and a new nomination starts empty. Editing the plan in place is out (signers sign exactly the plan they saw, DECISIONS.md "One frozen plan for every signature"); auto-release is out (the engine would drop a human's pending decision, and blocks are often transient).

Replace = reject iN, then nominate a prefilled new plan, from one place. Console-side, no rules change: a reject then a nomination, plus a read-only `replaces` on the dry run (POST /api/engage/options) so the form judges the new plan with iN treated as gone (world.engaged without iN). Not offered once iN is dispatched (abort is the card's). The replacer becomes the proposer and so cannot sign.

An atomic engine replace with a logged replaced_by link is a later option (new rules version, replay) only if the console gap (reject succeeds, nomination then fails) matters.
close_reason: Replace from the card and the form's platform step; read-only replaces on the dry run

title: Uniform task options: an explicit task catalog per node and one options generator for every goal
description: Owner agreed (2026-10-27) to make Murmur's tasking Lattice-shaped throughout: deterministic rules say what is feasible and rank it, an AI or a person chooses where judgment is needed, policy says which choices need a person. Today the pieces exist but are not uniform: tasks per platform are derived from the autopilot kind (crates/murmur-decide/src/catalog.rs) and sensors (sim/platforms.toml); feasibility is the engine's checks and dry run (preview_intent); ranked options exist only for identify (rules 21), nominations and satellite collections. Scope: (1) an explicit task catalog per node, each task with its parameters, limits and conditions, published to the console and MCP alike; (2) one options generator for every kind of goal (look at a contact, cover an area, patrol a route, relay a link), listing every vehicle that could do it with its pass or fail checks, its cost (time, endurance, p_failsafe) and what it would displace, read-only and deterministic; (3) the options shown and the choice made logged with the decision, so evaluation can tell a reasoned choice from always taking the first. Routine goals can be picked by the engine itself under policy (murmur-6xh). Builds after murmur-bia and murmur-6xh.

title: Replace up.sh with one Python stack supervisor
description:
Two stack starters exist: scripts/up.sh (bash, the live stack: SITL, stand-ins, tidewater, linkemu, bridge, contacts) and eval/stack.py (Python, eval stacks: holds Popen handles, readiness checks, ordered teardown, no SITL or tidewater). Port blocks are defined in four places (up.sh header, eval/launcher.py:99, eval/situation.py, eval/ports.py). make start goes launcher -> make -> up.sh -> swarm.py; teardown relies on per-service PID files and signals (gotchas: background up.sh ignores SIGINT, pkill -f kills your shell).

Plan, each step landable on its own:
1. One port-block registry (default, situation, eval) in one module, with the collision checks; up.sh, launcher, situation runner and eval read it.
2. Grow eval/stack.py to run the live stack: SITL via swarm.py's planner, tidewater serve/drive, and up.sh's checks (MURMUR_AT format, credentials, sim token, manifest written before the bridge). One entry point, e.g. python -m eval.stack up --fleet <name> --block default.
3. Launcher and situation_run call it in process; make targets become one-line wrappers; delete up.sh. Four layers become two.
4. Supervisor owns its children's lifetime (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, one PID file or the launcher API); make down signals that one process.

Not process-compose or Docker: the stack is dynamic (N SITL instances, conditional contacts and tidewater, manifest before bridge, HTTP readiness probes), so the logic stays in code anyway, and Docker adds UDP range and WSL networking friction. Keep the three toolchains (DECISIONS.md, Rust for the live path).

title: Headless G1 precision: P0 commands judged by truth on the headless side only
description:
Found by the independent verification of murmur-8ak's fix round 1 (2026-10-10). Not fixed: filed for a later round.

CRITERIA.md's precision (eval/headless/CRITERIA.md, as amended 2026-10-10) judges a human-tier P0 command (`safety.low_reserve`, `safety.stuck`) by whether its fault was real by truth: the vehicle's true charge, or a scripted stop. Only headless records carry the truth of our vehicles (`truth.ours`, the stand-ins' own state every 2 s); a full-stack record has none, so `metrics.p0_fault_real` returns None there and the proposal is listed as unjudged and left out of the proportion. The two sides therefore judge P0 commands differently.

No effect on G1 so far: in Harbor watch the P0 commands are auto-tier under the shipped watch policy, so none enters precision on either side. It would matter for any situation where a P0 command waits for a person.

Possible fix: record our vehicles' truth on the full stack (the stand-in engine's state, or the bridge's own reported battery as a stated proxy) and judge both sides alike, or keep P0 out of the gated precision on both sides; either needs a dated CRITERIA.md section.

title: Headless simulator: stand-in and bridge phases fixed across episodes; the playbook's first tick drawn wider than the full stack's
description:
Found by the independent verification of murmur-8ak's fix round 1 (2026-10-10). Not fixed: filed for a later round.

The headless simulator's process phases are the same in every episode, where the full stack's vary run to run:

- Battery report ages at the opening orders' checks are identical in every headless seed (0.90, 0.28 and 0.84 s for the three vehicles reported), against 0.3 to 1.3 s across the full-stack runs (reviewer's scratchpad/rev-headless/battery_age.py over logs/headless-g1/gate2 and gate2-headless in the murmur-8ak worktree). The stand-ins' start (`standins_start_s`, a median) and their stream phases are fixed; only the emulator's draws and the stand-ins' own draws vary.
- The playbook's first tick after `ai_start_s` is drawn uniformly over 0.711 to 1.590 s (the six calibration runs' range, seeds 101 to 106), while 19 of the 20 gate runs (seeds 1 to 20) came at 1.28 to 1.41 s (0.46 and 0.52 s in the other two). Gate seeds may not be fitted on: narrowing the range needs more calibration seeds (107 and up, CRITERIA.md's rule), then a dated CRITERIA.md section before any gate re-run.

Where it can matter: a check or a preview at a fact-age boundary (seed 18 of the G1 re-run: a 10.6 s battery report against the 10 s limit decided a proposal), and the phase of every playbook tick against the bridge's 1 s loops.

Possible fix: draw the stand-ins' start and the first tick per episode seed from distributions measured on more calibration runs.

title: Console: the agent ids that run the playbook are hard-coded (PLAYBOOK_AGENTS)
description: web/src/evidence.ts folds a rationale's evidence record only on a card proposed by an agent id in PLAYBOOK_AGENTS, which is hard-coded to ['agent-playbook'] (murmur-t8m fix round 2, so a model agent cannot hide text under the fold). A deployment that runs the playbook under another id (a second instance, a renamed roster) gets its records shown whole, not folded. The list could come from the bridge (its agent roster says which ids run the playbook) or from the console's config.

title: Playbook: a P0 card on an engaging platform comes back every 240 s while the signers let it expire
description: Found in the third review of murmur-t8m. Since fix round 2 a P0 command (safety.low_reserve, safety.stuck) on a platform with an engagement in play goes on and the bridge makes it a human card that stops the engagement if approved. If the signers let it expire, the expiry cooldown (2 min) and the approval wait (120 s) bring it back every 240 s; after a rejection, every 10 minutes. Bounded and per platform, but signers busy with the engagement may want a longer back-off for P0 cards on an engaging platform (for example doubling after each expiry, or none until the engagement ends). Repro: the reviewer's sim11.py, case V (cards at 0, 240, 480 s).

title: not_moving alerts: carry when the vehicle stopped, not only in the detail text
description: Found in the playbook's fix round 1 (murmur-t8m, review finding 4). A not_moving alert's since_t is the last state change of the order it is about (minutes before, for an order that ran a while), and how long the vehicle has not moved is only in the detail text ('NOT MOVING for 12s (aground or stuck?)'). An agent that debounces on since_t holds a vehicle on the first read; the playbook now counts 30 s from the first read in which it saw the alert, which is late by however long the stall ran before the alert reached it. A structured stalled_since_t (or not_moving_s) on the alert would let agents and the console time it from the stall. Not done in murmur-t8m: that round was not to change the bridge's alert semantics.

title: Auth: passkey login/step-up reserve a limiter slot with no drop guard (in_flight leaks on a dropped request, holding the id at BUSY); store read guard held across record_passkey_removed's audit append (auth.rs:1108-1113); sessions guard held into close_login (auth.rs:1358-1370)
Bridge: a wedged bridge ignores TERM (shutdown_signal is a tokio task); add a std signal thread or a progress watchdog that logs and exits
Console: a dropped declared hostile is drawn and listed as 'counted' in the keep-out though the engine exempts it
description: Seen live during the rules 16 merge: the fast boat, declared hostile, dropped after its effect, is listed in the tracks drawer and drawn on the map as 'counted within 27 km', while the engine exempts declared hostiles from keep-outs. The bridge sends lost_json regions for exempt contacts (crates/murmur-bridge/src/decision/engage.rs:2189); the console draws them (web/src/TracksPanel.tsx:442, web/src/trackLayers.ts:87). Either don't send regions for exempt contacts or mark them exempt in the console.

title: murmur-replay prints nothing for rules 16 (lost contacts, claims, confirmations, reinstatements)
description: ReplayReport has lost_contacts, lost_claims, lost_confirmed and lost_reinstated, but murmur-replay prints none of them (crates/murmur-decide/src/bin/murmur-replay.rs around line 362). Rules 15 prints UNSPENT: lines; rules 16 should print its own facts the same way.

title: Air tracker follow-ups: coordinated-turn model, EO/IR as angles only, 2D radar vertical beam, multi-observer air variant
description: From murmur-oho: (1) velocity in sustained turns stays overconfident when given (normalized error 4-97, given 0-23% of the time): a coordinated-turn model; (2) EO/IR on aircraft is still a full position fix, a passive sensor gives angles only; (3) a 2D radar's vertical beam limit is not modelled (a user decision: adding it hides aircraft overhead, a loosening); (4) a multi-observer air variant and turning aircraft in the keep-out measurement.

title: Rules 12 follow-ups: spent state across a restart; pointer and void-reason residuals
description: Focused re-check of rules 12 (df2ddda): (1, low-medium) the spent marker isn't carried across a restart (CarriedFrom/Debts carry owed values, pending logs and may_owe, and the closure removed the debt), so after a bridge-only restart or with real vehicles a spent platform is taskable and nominatable again while still carrying the engagement's lost-link action, which the next preload reads as its own values: carry spent uids in carried_from and replay-check them. (2) a corrupted pointer drops the chain behind it (recorded unknown, nothing held until written off); fall back to the newest log in the directory. (3) write_pointer syncs the file but not the directory: fsync the directory after the rename. (4) a pointer with two identical lines counts as unknown: accept it. (5) 'superseded' void reasons aren't checked against the log: check the named newer order exists on that vehicle. (6) may_owe comes from an unhashed fleet file: compare with <log>.fleet.json when at hand.

title: Follow-ups to rules 12: refuse nominations on platforms a failed carry may owe; an operator 'un-spend' override
description: Stated gaps of the rules 12 follow-ups (df2ddda): (1) a nomination on a platform a failed carry may owe (may_owe) is not refused; closing it needs another logged fact. (2) No override for a platform marked spent by its own effect that an operator believes survived (a miss): decide whether an engagement-authority operator may un-spend it, logged with a note, and what that requires (e.g. the platform heard and its own lost-link values verified). Also: may_owe comes from <log stem>.fleet.json, outside the hash chain; replay only checks it appears on failed carries (the start anchor binds it).

title: Space re-check: pass-time guard and replay read different clock instants; replay doesn't flag a pin change between loads
description: Focused re-check of rules 11 (9a3f69b), two lows: (1) recheck_space judges 'has the pass come' on one clock read while replay judges on the check.result timestamp (a later read): a probe with a clock moving 1 ms per read flagged an honest log ('a collect re-checked after its pass had come') at 1-2 ms before the pass. Stamp the check at the guard's instant (as fixed for cancel). (2) The engine API accepts a re-pinned segment as a new one and replay doesn't flag a pin change between two space.loaded events (the bridge no longer re-pins); flag a mid-log pin change. Note also: 'the engine never computes a cover' now applies under rules 10 and earlier too (behaviour change replay can't see).
close_reason: Merged to master (rules 13, SPACE_REPLAY_SINCE; reviewed, seven findings fixed)

title: Bridge clock::wall takes a global mutex per call: measure at 3-4k stand-ins
description: Re-check of 1b8082c: wall() (crates/murmur-bridge/src/clock.rs ~103-108) takes a global mutex and reads the OS clock on every call, several times per datagram. Microbenchmark: 49 ns single-threaded (22 ns before); 124-225 ns per call serialised at 4-16 threads (a ~4-8 M/s ceiling). Irrelevant at 100 vehicles; measure with scripts/measure.py at 3-4k stand-ins (murmur-pcb's scale) and, if it shows, make readers lock-free: steer once per tick and have readers extrapolate from an atomic segment.

title: Passkey login options leak which operators hold a passkey (decoy credential id length)
description: Security review of rules 10 (5f69c16): decoy_options (crates/murmur-auth/src/passkeys.rs ~225) emits a fixed 16-byte (22-char base64url) credential id, while real ids are whatever the authenticator chose (32 bytes for the virtual authenticator, longer for hardware keys). Unauthenticated POST /api/auth/login/passkey {operator} therefore shows by allowCredentials id length which operator ids exist and hold a passkey; login options issuance isn't rate-limited. Fix: make the decoy indistinguishable (length and count drawn like real ones, or a deterministic per-id decoy matching common lengths) and rate-limit options issuance per id. Low impact: ids are low-value and the engagement binding is untouched.
close_reason: Merged to master (rules 13, SPACE_REPLAY_SINCE; reviewed, seven findings fixed)

title: Lost-link restore owed by an expended platform stays UNRESTORED forever
description: Seen in the passkeys live run (rules 10 branch, 2026-10-05): an expended switchblade never answered the lost-link restore after its engagement, so replay reports UNRESTORED and the restore stays owed (inbox restore_pending, carried to the next run via .last-run). An expended (consumed) platform can't be restored; decide how the ledger closes it (e.g. an operator writes it off, logged, or the expended state closes the debt automatically with the reason), and make replay agree. Earlier behaviour, not from the passkeys change.
close_reason: Merged as decision rules 12 (REVIEW_FOLLOWUPS_SINCE) after review and a focused re-check (df2ddda).

title: Keep-out reach facts fail open for young tracks
description: Focused check of rules 9 (80d8469): a track under about 45 s old has no mean velocity, and one with no manoeuvre seen yet gets no manoeuvre region, so the keep-out falls back to the rules 8 single region (engage.rs track_reach). Stated in doc comments. Consider failing closed: treat a young track as possibly manoeuvring (reach at its domain's plausible top speed) until the facts exist. Needs the next rules version.
close_reason: Merged as decision rules 12 (REVIEW_FOLLOWUPS_SINCE) after review and a focused re-check (df2ddda).

title: Fix the scripted-operator set at run start (run.started) so replay checks each session against it
description: Re-check of the auth branch (e5ccf91): whether an operator is scripted is read from the credential file at each login and not recorded in run.started. Turning it off mid-run (murmur-auth scripted <op> off) ends that operator's sessions and the next login logs as 'password', so replay lists them under people; rewriting a session's 'password' as 'scripted' or back passes replay (forgery 14), caught only by anchors. Eval is unaffected (counts only op-study). Fix: log the scripted ids in run.started and have replay check each session's method against them (next rules version). Cosmetic, same review: when the per-session step-up limit trips, the 429 says 'too many failed attempts for this operator' though the limit is per session.
close_reason: Merged as decision rules 12 (REVIEW_FOLLOWUPS_SINCE) after review and a focused re-check (df2ddda).

title: After a crash, lost-link values carried from the earlier run's log hold no queued mission
description: Rules 7 (murmur-85l) holds a mission for a platform still owed its own lost-link values by an engagement of this run. Values carried from an earlier run's log (by empty, replay.rs ~269) hold nothing, because the log alone can't tell which vehicle they were preloaded on. So in exactly the crash case, a queued mission carried into the next run can fly over the preloaded fallback. The bridge already checks identity for carried restores; a bridge-fed hold for matching identities (with replay able to recompute it from logged facts) looks possible. Needs a rules version.
close_reason: Merged as decision rules 12 (REVIEW_FOLLOWUPS_SINCE) after review and a focused re-check (df2ddda).

title: E2E harnesses predate the rules 5 queue: approve queued orders, expect a submerged AUV patrol to go out
description: Found fixing murmur-0u7: sim/tests/standins_e2e.py approved an order the rules 5 queue was holding (202 queued; approving it is a 409). Its task() was fixed on the murmur-0u7 branch to approve only pending_approval and wait for a queued intent's tasking, but it still can't pass end to end: its second REMUS patrol, sent while submerged by design, is queued on the acoustic-modem link for up to 900 s (DECISIONS 'Reachable means heard'), so the harness's 10-02 expectation must change (expect queued, then surface, then dispatched, or assert the queue reason). The three SITL harnesses (standins_e2e_air.py, standins_e2e_plane_boat_sub.py, standins_e2e_blimp_ugv_sailboat.py) still approve any order without a tasking id and need the same task() fix; run them with SITL to confirm.
notes: From the re-check of 4c42d89: if approving a pending_approval intent puts it in the queue, the approve reply's tasking is null (api.rs ~319-324); standins_e2e.py and standins_tracker_e2e.py then fail on t['id'] instead of waiting. Fall through to the wait when tasking is null.

title: Bridge: name the .last-run log and its head in run.started so dropped carried restores are detectable
description: Review of the replay strictness branch (3ed31ba): replay can't detect a successor log with every carried platform.restore removed (forgery C3: exit 0, nothing said), because nothing in the log says a carry was due. Have the bridge record in run.started which .last-run log it read and that log's head (and whether it owed anything), so replay can require the carried restores. Changes what is logged: needs a rules version. Also from the same review: .last-run is rewritten even when the carry failed (crates/murmur-bridge/src/decision/engage.rs ~756), so an earlier log's debt drops out of the chain with only an inbox alert; keep pointing at the log still owed until its debt is carried or explicitly written off by an operator. And a bridge crash mid carry_from loop (engage.rs ~765-790) leaves a partial carried set, which replay's 'every owed platform carried' would reject: make the carry atomic or log it as one event.
notes: Also from the re-check of f070f5f: the bridge's restore carry (engage.rs carry_restores) trusts the .last-run log without replaying it or checking its anchors, unlike carry_over; murmur-replay can't check the carried values' log against its own anchors in the same run (a <stem>.anchors lookup or --prev-anchors would close forgery N1: predecessor rewritten and re-chained to owe the forged values, caught only by its anchors).
close_reason: Merged as decision rules 12 (REVIEW_FOLLOWUPS_SINCE) after review and a focused re-check (df2ddda).

title: A queued newer order abandons an engagement's intercept as a system stop and flies the fallback
description: Final review of rules 6 (present on master 5444976, not from the merge). A newer order queued for an engagement's platform makes supersede_queued abandon the engagement's unstarted intercept (crates/murmur-bridge/src/decision/queue.rs around 239); the engagement loop reads that as an intercept failure (engage.rs around 970), stops with cause 'system: the platform's intercept failed: abandoned ... (the newest order stands)' and commands its fallback. The same order dispatched instead stops it as 'superseded' with no fallback. Probe: a hold queued on a cut link aborted the engagement as system and its fallback RTL flew when the link returned while the operator's hold was still queued (log replays). The stop cause is mislabeled for evaluation (Phase G counts causes) and the operator's order is contradicted until it leaves the queue. Fix: treat a queued newer order like a dispatched one (superseded, no fallback), or decide explicitly and record it in DECISIONS.md.
close_reason: Merged as decision rules 7 (QUEUE_FOLLOWUPS_SINCE) after review, re-check and a third check: starts logged ahead; missions held (or refused for never-queued kinds) while a platform is owed its own lost-link values; an order queued, dispatched or refused for an engaging platform supersedes it without fallback; engine refuses requeue after a start; airship refusal text corrected.

title: Replay --prev doesn't check carried platform.restore values against what the predecessor owed
description: Final review of rules 6: --prev verifies intent.resumed only; carried platform.restore values (crates/murmur-decide/src/replay.rs around 390) are not compared with what the predecessor still owed. The two pointers can name different logs (.resume-<port>.json is deleted on a clean stop and has a 900 s window; .last-run-<port> is rewritten at every start, including MURMUR_RESUME=<log> or =0). Fix: when --prev is the log a carried restore names, check its values against owed_restores(prev).
close_reason: Merged (f070f5f) after review and re-check: replay rejects an op requeued after its start went out (per delivery; adopted vehicles after a resume too) and checks carried platform.restore values against the log they name, which must itself replay; absent or unnamed predecessors fail closed unless --trust-resumed.

title: Replay accepts op 'starting' followed by 'requeued'
description: Third review of the safe command queue, forgery Rf: murmur-replay accepts an op that logged 'starting' and then 'requeued', which the live bridge never writes (a start that may have gone out is never requeued). A consistency check, low severity: replay should flag it.

Without the link emulator, scripts/up.sh starts sim/swarm.py and the bridge at the same time, so the carry-over fleet identity check (crates/murmur-bridge/src/decision/queue.rs, around line 445) can read the previous run's sim/run/fleet.json. title: Align Morning Harbor Watch environmental forcing to the 2024 recording
description: Morning Harbor Watch replays NOAA AIS and six-minute station wind for 2024-06-14 15:00-16:00 UTC. Its first version deliberately uses no Tidewater service or historical current/tidal forcing; live wind supplies sensing/context, and existing 2026 terrain is static reference geometry only. Evaluate matching current fields, datum-correct tide/terrain and the same wind archive for live vehicle dynamics; keep cached offline provenance, missing data explicit and live/headless behavior comparable. Bundled MLLW tide predictions are context, not NAVD88 elevations. Do not silently reuse 2026 conditions.

title: Evaluate external integrations: TAK, HYDRIS, Aerostack2 and SwarmBox
description:
Owner request, 2026-10-29: record external integration options for future consideration. This is a backlog comparison, not approval to install these systems, connect physical vehicles, or replace Murmur's decision engine. No comparative performance testing has been done.

TAK / OpenTAKServer / FreeTAKServer: strongest near-term fit when additional observers, handsets or teams need the simulated picture. Murmur already exports vehicles and perceived contacts using CoT; inbound markers cannot task vehicles. Reuse existing murmur-q8k for geoid height, TLS/client certificates and actual TAK-client rendering validation. Validate affiliation, source uncertainty and staleness across the connection. No need to replace the Murmur decision console. Sources: crates/murmur-bridge/src/cot.rs; https://docs.opentakserver.io/ ; https://github.com/FreeTAKTeam/FreeTakServer .

HYDRIS: consider an optional external data connector, initially a read-only ADS-B or AIS experiment with recording and replay. Documented adapters include AIS/NMEA receivers or feeds, adsb.lol aircraft reports, ASTERIX CAT 062 radar tracks, TAK/CoT, MAVLink telemetry, Reolink/Axis cameras, ROS 2, Meshtastic and Space-Track. Its existing MAVLink integration is telemetry-only, not a replacement for Murmur's command executor. It does not provide sensor hardware, restricted network access, vendor credentials or satellite tasking simply by installing it. Compare the full dependency and data-mapping cost against one direct adapter before adoption. Use a separate observation path, preserve source identity, measured/received time, uncertainty, expiry and recording provenance, and keep Murmur's authority and audit semantics. A public traffic report is neither perfect truth nor a detection made by a simulated sensor. Define explicitly whether recorded traffic drives synthetic background motion or is an external observed track; retain seeded simulation for controlled evaluation. HYDRIS entity synchronization is not evidence of solved multi-sensor association. Sources: https://projectqai.github.io/docs/integration ; /integration/mavlink ; /integration/ais ; /integration/adsb ; /docs/developer/merge (all under projectqai.github.io/docs except the last full path).

Aerostack2: consider when research needs camera-driven behaviors, localization, motion planning or coordinated aerial missions beyond existing autopilot tasks. A ROS 2 autonomy framework with platform interfaces; it may sit above an autopilot, rather than replace its stabilization, navigation and mission execution. Do not assume a supported ArduPilot adapter without verification. Start with one simulated platform if this research need appears; keep Murmur authorization upstream. Sources: https://aerostack2.github.io/ ; https://aerostack2.github.io/_03_aerial_platforms/index.html ; https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/companion-computers.html .

SwarmBox: consider for actual inter-vehicle coordination research: pluggable behavior algorithms, centralized/decentralized communication arrangements, synchronized distributed logs and an analyzer correlating GCS events, inter-agent latency/loss, position discrepancies and low-level flight logs. This complements Murmur's decision audit but duplicates parts of its test harness. Current homepage lists ArduPilot support as planned, so PX4/ROS integration work is material. Possible smaller experiment: evaluate analysis/export compatibility before adopting its runtime. Sources: https://compsec.postech.ac.kr/swarmbox/ ; https://compsec.postech.ac.kr/assets/publications/lee:swarmbox.pdf .

MAVSDK / pymavswarm: evaluate only against a concrete new backend or command-maintenance problem; no demonstrated advantage from replacing existing link-aware retries, mission upload, telemetry lifecycle and restart recovery. Crazyswarm2 / Skybrush: revisit only for Bitcraze aerial-team or drone-show experiments. Auterion / Lattice: interoperability would require an actual available endpoint and access agreement; not needed for the present open simulation. Existing ArduPilot SITL remains the foundation; PX4 is a possible additional backend, not an automatic improvement.

Reconsideration criteria: name the source/system, available access, missing capability, data semantics and clock model, measurable benefit, maintenance cost and preservation of replay and human authority. The largest access barrier is not necessarily classification: standard protocol support, actual accessible equipment/feed, licensing/vendor access and authority to task are separate questions. Murmur remains a working draft with no validated human-study findings.
notes: Owner decision 2026-10-29: defer SwarmBox until we start running real swarms (actual coordinated multi-vehicle behavior; this is not authorization to connect hardware). Defer HYDRIS until live demos or similar live external-data integration is wanted. Neither is needed for the immediate historical-data scenario work. Revisit these explicit triggers rather than treating either as a current dependency.

title: Headless runner: no cancel of an opening order a scripted id approved at submission (the live runner cancels it)
description:
Found in murmur-8ak's review (fix round 1, unaddressed edge case; filed 2026-10-10). Not fixed.

The live situation runner (eval/situation_run.py `issue_order`) checks each opening order op-setup submits: if the answer shows it approved at submission by a scripted id (`self_authorized`: a fact changed between the dry run and the submission), it cancels the intent unless it went out already (`undo_self_authorized`, `POST /api/intents/{id}/cancel`) and records a loud problem. The headless runner (eval/headless/episode.py `Runner.issue_orders`) submits the same way after the same dry run but never makes that check or cancel.

No effect in Harbor watch or the families so far: the dry run and the submission happen at one simulated instant, so the facts cannot change between them and the case cannot arise headless as built. It would if the runner ever waited between the two. Fix: port `self_authorized` and `undo_self_authorized` into `Runner.issue_orders` (record `self_authorized` in the order's record as live does) and test it with a stubbed answer.

title: Headless session adapter: a protocol error raises RuntimeError, the live session McpError
description:
Found in murmur-8ak's review (fix round 1, unaddressed edge case; filed 2026-10-10). Not fixed.

On an MCP protocol error (an unknown tool, invalid parameters), the live session (agents/policy_agent.py `AgentSession.call` through agents/scripted_agent.py `call`, the MCP SDK's `ClientSession.call_tool`) raises the SDK's `McpError`; the headless session adapter (eval/headless/sim.py `HeadlessSession._call`) raises `RuntimeError(<protocol error message>)`. A tool-level error (`isError`) raises `RuntimeError("<tool>: <error>")` on both sides, as it should.

No effect today: the playbook's engine catches `Exception` around every session call. A client that catches `McpError` specifically would behave differently headless. Fix: raise `mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError` with the same `ErrorData` (code and message) the SDK would build, and add the case to eval/headless/tests/test_session.py.

title: Headless simulator: run.started and the first anchor stamped at t = 0, about 1.02 s before live
description:
Found by the independent verification of murmur-8ak's fix round 1 (2026-10-10). Not fixed: filed for a later round.

In the headless simulator, the bridge's `run.started` audit event and its first anchor (`why: start`) are stamped at t = 0 (the simulator builds the decision layer with `Decision::load` at the episode's start), while on the full stack the decision layer starts about 1.02 s after the situation's zero (first anchor 1.016 to 1.048 s over calibration runs 101 to 106 and the gate runs). Fix round 1 made the bridge's loops start, and its sockets answer, at `bridge_start_s` (1.024 s), but `Decision::load` still runs at 0, so its start stamp and the anchors' first entry are about 1 s early against live.

Effect seen: none on the playbook's proposals or the G1 metrics (nothing reads the start stamp); audit logs compared across the two sides differ there. Fix: build the decision layer at `bridge_start_s` (crates/murmur-headless/src/sim/mod.rs `assemble`), keeping the order main.rs uses.

title: Lost-contact acceptance checks the step-up before authority (403) and acceptability (409); rules 15's un-spend does the opposite
description: crates/murmur-bridge/src/api.rs accept_unknown with a track: the password or passkey step-up is asked before the 403/409 checks, following rules 6's lost-vehicle precedent; rules 15 chose the opposite order for un-spend so a refused act never takes a password. Align them (likely the rules 15 order for both); no recorded decision either way. From the rules 16 merge review.

description: web/src/EngagePanel.tsx:224 shows one failing check per platform in the list, so with both keep_out_tracks (rules 16) and fallback_preload (rules 15) failing, fallback_preload only appears once the platform is chosen. Predates the rules 16 merge; show every failing check (or a count).

title: Keep-out explanation: the 0.25 s window scan can miss a narrow window or a dip between grid points
description: Re-check of 0472a71 (built deliberately, not seen on realistic pictures): (1) a gap narrower than the grid (keepout.rs ~1101): blocked before t0+50.05 s and after t0+50.15 s, the explanation says no effect time passes, but the platform at 360.79 m lands at +50.10 s and passes; (2) a dip between grid points (~1114): an 80 m/s aircraft grazes the clearance only between 30.0 and 30.25 s (274.98 m vs 275.05 m at the grid points), the explanation says within 300 m, but at 121 m the dry run fails by 2 cm. Never unsafe (the engine re-checks at submission). Fix: say 'on a 0.25 s grid' in the no-effect-time sentence and console line, and require ~0.3 m margin at grid points (bounds the dip for anything up to 100 m/s).

title: MURMUR_RATE without MURMUR_AT: bridge ScenarioClock is identity while /api/space/catalog reports the rate
description: Seen by the space follow-ups agent (2026-10-06): with MURMUR_RATE=10 but no MURMUR_AT, the bridge's ScenarioClock::map() is the identity while /api/space/catalog reports rate 10. The log stayed self-consistent in its run; check whether any consumer (console, space answers, linkemu) assumes the rate and could disagree, and either apply the rate without MURMUR_AT (from the bridge clock at start) or refuse/ignore MURMUR_RATE without it, stated.
notes: Review of the space follow-ups (2026-10-06) confirmed it: with MURMUR_RATE=10 and no MURMUR_AT, /api/space/catalog reports {rate: 10, source: wall clock} while the engine's map is the identity. No wrong engine decision (space API and engine both at 1x), but the console's useScenarioNow (web/src/space.ts ~270) runs its clock at 10x between refreshes (a human can read a pass as come or gone when it isn't), and the stand-ins' GNSS and currents clock (murmur-standins/src/gnss.rs ~742) runs at 10x from wall start. Make all three agree.

title: Eval link-cut windows still carry the monotonic drift
description: Re-check of 1b8082c: eval's cut windows are the emulator's start plus at_s on its monotonic clock (eval/metrics.py ~256, ~1213), so in the early-boot drift state they are off by up to 2.1% of at_s (~5 s at 240 s). Master had the same error; the docs call them wall-clock windows. Map them through the bridge's anchors (utc beside bridge time) or have the emulator log its event times on the bridge's clock; fix the doc wording.

title: Refusal reason should name an older queued order that still stands on the same vehicles
description: Third check of rules 7 (486fc49): a mission refused because its platform is still owed its own lost-link values supersedes engagements but leaves older queued orders in place (safer when the older order is a hold or rtl). Probe: scenario 67 under the orbit-never-queued policy; op-1's hold queued at t=44 supersedes the engagement; op-1's orbit at t=50 is refused; when the link returns the older hold goes at t=71. Under dispatch semantics the newer order would have voided it; here the refusal text doesn't tell the operator the older order still stands. Add a clause naming it. Logged text: needs the next rules version.
